items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Gennady Goldstein was a young alto player and we started to hang out a bit.

ctx.x: And then went on to Deblice and Kiev and Leningrad. Leningrad was the best. We had a jam session at the Leningrad University, and uh Gennady Goldstein was a young alto player and we started to hang out a bit. And he came to my uh came to my hotel and I wanted to give him a bathrobe that I had. A nice, you know, I wanted to give him something and I had a brand new bathrobe that I never wore, and he said, “ I’d love it but if I leave the hotel with a gift from you, the police will take it away.” Because everybody…

handed a check. And we had Life magazine and the A.P., all the press services, European press, you know, it was very embarrassing, and it was, made, it was kind of a scandal in the States about the Benny Goodman band being on strike. We weren’t really on strike; we just wanted to get paid and Benny made us wait until the very last concert, you know. But the Russians got even with him, you know. Because they, Benny was supposed to play, I dunno, the Brahm’s or some some classical piece, I don’t remember what it…
